title: Thin answers
exercises: A candidate who answers in one line. Very little evidence. Expected: mostly neutral scores, few quotes, low coverage — honest neutrals, never invented detail.

exchanges.question: Tell me about a problem you'd never seen before — how did you get your arms around it?
exchanges.answer: I looked it up and asked a colleague. It got sorted.

exchanges.question: How do you keep track of your work when several things are due at once?
exchanges.answer: I use the ticket queue. Oldest first, mostly.

exchanges.question: Walk me through a working day that suits you — where does working with other people fit in?
exchanges.answer: Normal day. Some people, some on my own. Either is fine.

exchanges.question: Tell me about a real disagreement with a teammate — how did it play out?
exchanges.answer: Can't think of one really. We usually just agree.

exchanges.question: Tell me about a time the pressure got real — a deadline slipping, something breaking. What did you do?
exchanges.answer: Just got on with it. It was fine in the end.

exchanges.question: Think of a stretch of work you were genuinely glad to be doing — what made it worth it: calling the shots, getting properly good at something, or the people around you?
exchanges.answer: The people I suppose. It was a decent team.

exchanges.question: What part of a working week leaves you with more energy than you started with — and what part drains it?
exchanges.answer: Fridays are good. Mondays less so. Nothing specific.

exchanges.question: Tell me about a place you worked that just felt right — what was it about how they ran things?
exchanges.answer: My last place was alright. They left you alone to do the job, which I liked.
